sanskrit: mahāmerur mahākāśo jaladaḥ kumudottaraḥ jaladhārāt paro rājan sukumāra iti smṛtaḥ
english: Mahāmeru, Mahākāśa, Jalada, and Kumudottara, O king; and beyond Jaladhāra is the one remembered as Sukumāra.

sanskrit: raivatasya tu kaumāraḥ śyāmasya tu maṇīcakaḥ kesarasyātha modākī pareṇa tu mahāpumān
english: For Raivata there is Kaumāra, for Śyāma there is Maṇīcaka, for Kesara there is Modākī, and beyond that the great Mahāpuruṣa.

sanskrit: parivārya tu kauravya dairghyaṃ hrasvatvam eva ca jambūdvīpena vikhyātas tasya madhye mahādrumaḥ
english: Encircling it, O Kaurava, in its length and breadth, it is famed in proportion to Jambūdvīpa; and in its midst stands a great tree.

sanskrit: śāko nāma mahārāja tasya dvīpasya madhyagaḥ tatra puṇyā janapadāḥ pūjyate tatra śaṃkaraḥ
english: It is named Śāka, O great king, standing at the center of that island. There the lands are holy, and there Śaṃkara is worshipped.

sanskrit: tatra gacchanti siddhāś ca cāraṇā daivatāni ca dhārmikāś ca prajā rājaṃś catvāro 'tīva bhārata
english: There go the Siddhas, the Cāraṇas, and the gods; and righteous are the people there, O king, the four classes exceedingly so, O Bhārata.

sanskrit: varṇāḥ svakarmaniratā na ca steno 'tra dṛśyate dīrghāyuṣo mahārāja jarāmṛtyuvivarjitāḥ
english: The classes are devoted each to its own duty, and no thief is seen there; long-lived are they, O great king, free from old age and death.

sanskrit: prajās tatra vivardhante varṣāsv iva samudragāḥ nadyaḥ puṇyajalās tatra gaṅgā ca bahudhāgatiḥ
english: The people there flourish like rivers flowing to the sea in the rains; the streams there are of holy water, and the Gaṅgā runs in many courses.

sanskrit: sukumārī kumārī ca sītā kāverakā tathā mahānadī ca kauravya tathā maṇijalā nadī ikṣuvardhanikā caiva tathā bharatasattama
english: Sukumārī and Kumārī, Sītā and Kāverakā, the Mahānadī too, O Kaurava, and the river Maṇijalā, and Ikṣuvardhanikā as well, O best of the Bharatas.

sanskrit: tataḥ pravṛttāḥ puṇyodā nadyaḥ kurukulodvaha sahasrāṇāṃ śatāny eva yato varṣati vāsavaḥ
english: From there flow forth holy-watered rivers, O upholder of the Kuru line, hundreds upon thousands of them, wherever Vāsava sends his rain.

sanskrit: na tāsāṃ nāmadheyāni parimāṇaṃ tathaiva ca śakyate parisaṃkhyātuṃ puṇyās tā hi saridvarāḥ
english: Their names and likewise their number cannot be reckoned in full, for they are holy, those finest of rivers.

sanskrit: tatra puṇyā janapadāś catvāro lokasaṃmatāḥ magāś ca maśakāś caiva mānasā mandagās tathā
english: There are four holy lands, esteemed by the world: the Magas and the Maśakas, the Mānasas and the Mandagas.

sanskrit: magā brāhmaṇabhūyiṣṭhāḥ svakarmaniratā nṛpa maśakeṣu tu rājanyā dhārmikāḥ sarvakāmadāḥ
english: The Magas are mostly brāhmaṇas, devoted to their own duty, O king; among the Maśakas dwell kṣatriyas, righteous and granting every desire.

sanskrit: mānaseṣu mahārāja vaiśyāḥ karmopajīvinaḥ sarvakāmasamāyuktāḥ śūrā dharmārthaniścitāḥ śūdrās tu mandage nityaṃ puruṣā dharmaśīlinaḥ
english: Among the Mānasas, O great king, are vaiśyas who live by their work, endowed with every wish, valiant, resolute in dharma and wealth; and in Mandaga ever dwell śūdras, men of righteous conduct.

sanskrit: na tatra rājā rājendra na daṇḍo na ca daṇḍikāḥ svadharmeṇaiva dharmaṃ ca te rakṣanti parasparam
english: There is no king there, O lord of kings, no rod of punishment nor those who wield it; by their own dharma alone they guard one another's righteousness.

sanskrit: etāvad eva śakyaṃ tu tasmin dvīpe prabhāṣitum etāvad eva śrotavyaṃ śākadvīpe mahaujasi
english: This much only can be told of that island, and this much only is to be heard concerning the mighty Śākadvīpa.

sanskrit: saṃjaya uvāca uttareṣu tu kauravya dvīpeṣu śrūyate kathā yathāśrutaṃ mahārāja bruvatas tan nibodha me
english: Saṃjaya said: Of the islands to the north, O Kaurava, a tale is heard; as I have heard it, O great king, hear it now from me as I tell it.

sanskrit: ghṛtatoyaḥ samudro 'tra dadhimaṇḍodako 'paraḥ surodaḥ sāgaraś caiva tathānyo gharmasāgaraḥ
english: Here is a sea whose waters are clarified butter, another whose waters are curds and whey, an ocean of wine, and yet another, a sea of warm water.

sanskrit: paraspareṇa dviguṇāḥ sarve dvīpā narādhipa sarvataś ca mahārāja parvataiḥ parivāritāḥ
english: Each is double the last, O ruler of men, all the islands; and on every side, O great king, they are girded round by mountains.

sanskrit: gauras tu madhyame dvīpe girir mānaḥśilo mahān parvataḥ paścimaḥ kṛṣṇo nārāyaṇanibho nṛpa
english: In the middle island stands a great mountain, white, of realgar; and to the west a dark mountain, resembling Nārāyaṇa, O king.

sanskrit: tatra ratnāni divyāni svayaṃ rakṣati keśavaḥ prajāpatim upāsīnaḥ prajānāṃ vidadhe sukham
english: There Keśava himself guards the divine jewels, and, attending upon Prajāpati, ordains the welfare of the creatures.

sanskrit: kuśadvīpe kuśastambo madhye janapadasya ha saṃpūjyate śalmaliś ca dvīpe śālmalike nṛpa
english: In Kuśadvīpa a clump of kuśa-grass, at the center of the land, is held in worship; and the śalmali tree on the island Śālmalika, O king.

sanskrit: krauñcadvīpe mahākrauñco girī ratnacayākaraḥ saṃpūjyate mahārāja cāturvarṇyena nityadā
english: In Krauñcadvīpa the great mountain Krauñca, a mine heaped with jewels, is worshipped ever, O great king, by all four classes.

sanskrit: gomandaḥ parvato rājan sumahān sarvadhātumān yatra nityaṃ nivasati śrīmān kamalalocanaḥ mokṣibhiḥ saṃstuto nityaṃ prabhur nārāyaṇo hariḥ
english: There is the great mountain Gomanda, O king, rich in every mineral, where the glorious lotus-eyed Lord dwells forever, ever praised by those who seek release, the lord Nārāyaṇa Hari.

sanskrit: kuśadvīpe tu rājendra parvato vidrumaiś citaḥ sudhāmā nāma durdharṣo dvitīyo hemaparvataḥ
english: In Kuśadvīpa, O lord of kings, is a mountain studded with coral, named Sudhāman, hard to assail; and a second, the golden mountain.

sanskrit: dyutimān nāma kauravya tṛtīyaḥ kumudo giriḥ caturthaḥ puṣpavān nāma pañcamas tu kuśeśayaḥ
english: Named Dyutimat, O Kaurava; third, the mountain Kumuda; fourth, the one named Puṣpavat; and fifth, Kuśeśaya.

sanskrit: ṣaṣṭho harigirir nāma ṣaḍ ete parvatottamāḥ teṣām antaraviṣkambho dviguṇaḥ pravibhāgaśaḥ
english: Sixth is the one named Harigiri; these six are the foremost of mountains, and the span between them, region by region, is double each preceding.

sanskrit: audbhidaṃ prathamaṃ varṣaṃ dvitīyaṃ veṇumaṇḍalam tṛtīyaṃ vai rathākāraṃ caturthaṃ pālanaṃ smṛtam
english: The first region is Audbhida, the second Veṇumaṇḍala, the third indeed Rathākāra, and the fourth is remembered as Pālana.

sanskrit: dhṛtimat pañcamaṃ varṣaṃ ṣaṣṭhaṃ varṣaṃ prabhākaram saptamaṃ kāpilaṃ varṣaṃ saptaite varṣapuñjakāḥ
english: Dhṛtimat is the fifth region, Prabhākara the sixth, and Kāpila the seventh region; these are the seven clusters of regions.

sanskrit: eteṣu devagandharvāḥ prajāś ca jagatīśvara viharanti ramante ca na teṣu mriyate janaḥ
english: In these the gods, the gandharvas, and the people, O lord of the earth, roam and take their delight, and no one there dies.

sanskrit: na teṣu dasyavaḥ santi mlecchajātyo 'pi vā nṛpa gauraprāyo janaḥ sarvaḥ sukumāraś ca pārthiva
english: In them there are no robbers, nor any of barbarian birth, O king; all the folk are fair of hue and delicate, O Pārtha.

sanskrit: avaśiṣṭeṣu varṣeṣu vakṣyāmi manujeśvara yathāśrutaṃ mahārāja tad avyagramanāḥ śṛṇu
english: Concerning the remaining regions I shall speak, O lord of men, as I have heard it, O great king; hear it with an untroubled mind.

sanskrit: krauñcadvīpe mahārāja krauñco nāma mahāgiriḥ krauñcāt paro vāmanako vāmanād andhakārakaḥ
english: In Krauñcadvīpa, O great king, is the great mountain named Krauñca; beyond Krauñca is Vāmanaka, and beyond Vāmana, Andhakāraka.

sanskrit: andhakārāt paro rājan mainākaḥ parvatottamaḥ mainākāt parato rājan govindo girir uttamaḥ
english: Beyond Andhakāra, O king, is Maināka, foremost of mountains; and beyond Maināka, O king, the lofty mountain Govinda.

sanskrit: govindāt tu paro rājan nibiḍo nāma parvataḥ paras tu dviguṇas teṣāṃ viṣkambho vaṃśavardhana
english: And beyond Govinda, O king, is a mountain named Nibiḍa; the span of each is double the last, O increaser of your line.

sanskrit: deśāṃs tatra pravakṣyāmi tan me nigadataḥ śṛṇu krauñcasya kuśalo deśo vāmanasya manonugaḥ
english: I shall tell you the countries there; hear me as I declare them. The country of Krauñca is Kuśala, that of Vāmana is Manonuga.

sanskrit: manonugāt paraś coṣṇo deśaḥ kurukulodvaha uṣṇāt paraḥ prāvarakaḥ prāvarād andhakārakaḥ
english: Beyond Manonuga is the country Uṣṇa, O upholder of the Kuru line; beyond Uṣṇa is Prāvaraka, and beyond Prāvara, Andhakāraka.

sanskrit: andhakārakadeśāt tu munideśaḥ paraḥ smṛtaḥ munideśāt paraś caiva procyate dundubhisvanaḥ
english: Beyond the country of Andhakāraka is remembered the country of Muni; and beyond the country of Muni is named Dundubhisvana.

sanskrit: siddhacāraṇasaṃkīrṇo gauraprāyo janādhipa ete deśā mahārāja devagandharvasevitāḥ
english: Thronged with Siddhas and Cāraṇas, its people mostly fair of hue, O lord of men; these countries, O great king, are frequented by gods and gandharvas.

sanskrit: puṣkare puṣkaro nāma parvato maṇiratnamān tatra nityaṃ nivasati svayaṃ devaḥ prajāpatiḥ
english: In Puṣkara is a mountain named Puṣkara, rich in gems and jewels; there the god Prajāpati himself dwells forever.

sanskrit: taṃ paryupāsate nityaṃ devāḥ sarve maharṣibhiḥ vāgbhir manonukūlābhiḥ pūjayanto janādhipa
english: Upon him all the gods, with the great seers, ever wait in attendance, honoring him with words that gladden the heart, O lord of men.

sanskrit: jambūdvīpāt pravartante ratnāni vividhāny uta dvīpeṣu teṣu sarveṣu prajānāṃ kurunandana
english: From Jambūdvīpa proceed jewels of many kinds, indeed, to all those islands, for the people, O joy of the Kurus.

sanskrit: viprāṇāṃ brahmacaryeṇa satyena ca damena ca ārogyāyuḥpramāṇābhyāṃ dviguṇaṃ dviguṇaṃ tataḥ
english: Through the brāhmaṇas' chastity, their truth, and their self-restraint, in measure of health and length of life it is double and ever doubling thereafter.

sanskrit: eko janapado rājan dvīpeṣv eteṣu bhārata uktā janapadā yeṣu dharmaś caikaḥ pradṛśyate
english: There is but one community, O king, in all these islands, O Bhārata, the lands of which I have spoken, where a single dharma is seen.

sanskrit: īśvaro daṇḍam udyamya svayam eva prajāpatiḥ dvīpān etān mahārāja rakṣaṃs tiṣṭhati nityadā
english: The Lord himself, Prajāpati, raising the rod of rule, O great king, stands ever guarding these islands.

sanskrit: sa rājā sa śivo rājan sa pitā sa pitāmahaḥ gopāyati naraśreṣṭha prajāḥ sajaḍapaṇḍitāḥ
english: He is king, he is the auspicious one, O king; he is father, he is grandfather; he shelters, O best of men, the people, both the dull and the wise.

sanskrit: bhojanaṃ cātra kauravya prajāḥ svayam upasthitam siddham eva mahārāja bhuñjate tatra nityadā
english: And here, O Kaurava, the people partake of food that comes to them of itself, already prepared, O great king, ever there.

sanskrit: tataḥ paraṃ samā nāma dṛśyate lokasaṃsthitiḥ caturaśrā mahārāja trayas triṃśat tu maṇḍalam
english: Beyond that is seen a region of the world named Samā, four-cornered, O great king, with a circuit of thirty-three.

sanskrit: tatra tiṣṭhanti kauravya catvāro lokasaṃmatāḥ diggajā bharataśreṣṭha vāmanairāvatādayaḥ supratīkas tathā rājan prabhinnakaraṭāmukhaḥ
english: There stand, O Kaurava, four elephants of the quarters, esteemed by the world, O best of the Bharatas, Vāmana, Airāvata, and the rest, and Supratīka too, O king, his cheeks and face streaming with rut.

sanskrit: tasyāhaṃ parimāṇaṃ tu na saṃkhyātum ihotsahe asaṃkhyātaḥ sa nityaṃ hi tiryag ūrdhvam adhas tathā
english: Its measure I cannot venture to reckon here, for it is forever beyond counting, across, above, and below alike.

sanskrit: tatra vai vāyavo vānti digbhyaḥ sarvābhya eva ca asaṃbādhā mahārāja tān nigṛhṇanti te gajāḥ
english: There indeed the winds blow from all the quarters, unobstructed, O great king, and those elephants take them in.

sanskrit: puṣkaraiḥ padmasaṃkāśair varṣmavadbhir mahāprabhaiḥ te śanaiḥ punar evāśu vāyūn muñcanti nityaśaḥ
english: With their trunks, like lotuses, broad and of mighty splendor, they then slowly, yet swiftly again, release the winds without end.

sanskrit: śvasadbhir mucyamānās tu diggajair iha mārutāḥ āgacchanti mahārāja tatas tiṣṭhanti vai prajāḥ
english: Released by the breathing elephants of the quarters, the winds come hither, O great king, and thereby the creatures live on.

sanskrit: dhṛtarāṣṭra uvāca paro vai vistaro 'tyarthaṃ tvayā saṃjaya kīrtitaḥ darśitaṃ dvīpasaṃsthānam uttaraṃ brūhi saṃjaya
english: Dhṛtarāṣṭra said: A vast expanse indeed have you recounted to excess, O Saṃjaya; you have shown the disposition of the islands. Now tell me what is beyond, O Saṃjaya.

sanskrit: saṃjaya uvāca uktā dvīpā mahārāja grahān me śṛṇu tattvataḥ svarbhānuḥ kauravaśreṣṭha yāvad eṣa prabhāvataḥ
english: Saṃjaya said: The islands have been told, O great king; now hear of the planets truly from me: Svarbhānu, O best of the Kauravas, how great he is in his might.

sanskrit: parimaṇḍalo mahārāja svarbhānuḥ śrūyate grahaḥ yojanānāṃ sahasrāṇi viṣkambho dvādaśāsya vai
english: Round in shape, O great king, the planet Svarbhānu is said to be; its diameter is full twelve thousand yojanas.

sanskrit: pariṇāhena ṣaṭtriṃśad vipulatvena cānagha ṣaṣṭim āhuḥ śatāny asya budhāḥ paurāṇikās tathā
english: In girth six and thirty thousand, and in breadth, O sinless one, the learned and the masters of the old lore declare it six thousand.

sanskrit: candramās tu sahasrāṇi rājann ekādaśa smṛtaḥ viṣkambheṇa kuruśreṣṭha trayastriṃśat tu maṇḍalam ekonaṣaṣṭir vaipulyāc chītaraśmer mahātmanaḥ
english: The moon, O king, is remembered as eleven thousand in diameter, O best of the Kurus, and thirty-three thousand in circuit, fifty-nine thousand in breadth, the great cool-rayed one.

sanskrit: sūryas tv aṣṭau sahasrāṇi dve cānye kurunandana viṣkambheṇa tato rājan maṇḍalaṃ triṃśataṃ samam
english: The sun is ten thousand—eight thousand and two more, O joy of the Kurus—in diameter; and thence, O king, its circuit is a full thirty thousand.

sanskrit: aṣṭapañcāśataṃ rājan vipulatvena cānagha śrūyate paramodāraḥ pataṃgo 'sau vibhāvasuḥ etat pramāṇam arkasya nirdiṣṭam iha bhārata
english: Fifty-eight thousand, O king, in breadth, O sinless one, that most exalted soaring one of light is said to be; such is the measure of the sun declared here, O Bhārata.

sanskrit: sa rāhuś chādayaty etau yathākālaṃ mahattayā candrādityau mahārāja saṃkṣepo 'yam udāhṛtaḥ
english: That Rāhu, by reason of his greatness, eclipses these two in their season, the moon and the sun, O great king; this is the account told in brief.

sanskrit: ity etat te mahārāja pṛcchataḥ śāstracakṣuṣā sarvam uktaṃ yathātattvaṃ tasmāc chamam avāpnuhi
english: Thus, O great king, to you who asked, all has been told according to the truth, with the eye of the scriptures; therefore attain to peace.

sanskrit: yathādṛṣṭaṃ mayā proktaṃ saniryāṇam idaṃ jagat tasmād āśvasa kauravya putraṃ duryodhanaṃ prati
english: This world, with its goings-forth, I have told as I have seen it; therefore take comfort, O Kaurava, concerning your son Duryodhana.

sanskrit: śrutvedaṃ bharataśreṣṭha bhūmiparva manonugam śrīmān bhavati rājanyaḥ siddhārthaḥ sādhusaṃmataḥ āyur balaṃ ca vīryaṃ ca tasya tejaś ca vardhate
english: Having heard this Section of the Earth, O best of the Bharatas, pleasing to the mind, the prince becomes glorious, his purpose fulfilled, esteemed by the good; and his life, strength, valor, and splendor increase.

sanskrit: yaḥ śṛṇoti mahīpāla parvaṇīdaṃ yatavrataḥ prīyante pitaras tasya tathaiva ca pitāmahāḥ
english: Whoever, O ruler of the earth, hears this on a parva-day, firm in his vows, his fathers are gladdened, and so too his forefathers.

sanskrit: idaṃ tu bhārataṃ varṣaṃ yatra vartāmahe vayam pūrvaṃ pravartate puṇyaṃ tat sarvaṃ śrutavān asi
english: But this region of Bhārata, wherein we dwell, holy from of old, now unfolds; all of it you have now heard.

sanskrit: vaiśaṃpāyana uvāca atha gāvalgaṇir dhīmān samarād etya saṃjayaḥ pratyakṣadarśī sarvasya bhūtabhavyabhaviṣyavit
english: Vaiśaṃpāyana said: Then the wise Saṃjaya, son of Gavalgaṇa, having come from the battle, an eyewitness of all, knower of past, present, and to come,

sanskrit: dhyāyate dhṛtarāṣṭrāya sahasopetya duḥkhitaḥ ācaṣṭa nihataṃ bhīṣmaṃ bharatānām amadhyamam
english: approaching in haste, grieving, declared to the brooding Dhṛtarāṣṭra that Bhīṣma, the foremost among the Bharatas, had been slain.

sanskrit: saṃjayo 'haṃ mahārāja namas te bharatarṣabha hato bhīṣmaḥ śāṃtanavo bharatānāṃ pitāmahaḥ
english: "I am Saṃjaya, O great king; homage to you, O bull of the Bharatas. Bhīṣma, son of Śaṃtanu, the grandsire of the Bharatas, is slain.

sanskrit: kakudaṃ sarvayodhānāṃ dhāma sarvadhanuṣmatām śaratalpagataḥ so 'dya śete kurupitāmahaḥ
english: The crest of all warriors, the abode of all who bear the bow, that grandsire of the Kurus lies today upon a bed of arrows.

sanskrit: yasya vīryaṃ samāśritya dyūtaṃ putras tavākarot sa śete nihato rājan saṃkhye bhīṣmaḥ śikhaṇḍinā
english: He upon whose valor relying your son made bold to play at dice—he, Bhīṣma, lies slain, O king, in the fray by Śikhaṇḍin.

sanskrit: yaḥ sarvān pṛthivīpālān samavetān mahāmṛdhe jigāyaikarathenaiva kāśipuryāṃ mahārathaḥ
english: He who, in a great battle at the city of Kāśi, vanquished all the rulers of the earth gathered together, with a single chariot, that mighty car-warrior—

sanskrit: jāmadagnyaṃ raṇe rāmam āyodhya vasusaṃbhavaḥ na hato jāmadagnyena sa hato 'dya śikhaṇḍinā
english: he, born of the Vasus, who fought Rāma the son of Jamadagni in combat and was not slain by the son of Jamadagni, is today slain by Śikhaṇḍin.

sanskrit: mahendrasadṛśaḥ śaurye sthairye ca himavān iva samudra iva gāmbhīrye sahiṣṇutve dharāsamaḥ
english: Like great Indra in prowess, like Himavat in steadfastness, like the ocean in depth, in forbearance the equal of the earth—

sanskrit: śaradaṃṣṭro dhanurvaktraḥ khaḍgajihvo durāsadaḥ narasiṃhaḥ pitā te 'dya pāñcālyena nipātitaḥ
english: his fangs his arrows, his mouth the bow, his tongue the sword, unassailable, that man-lion, your father, has today been struck down by the Pāñcāla prince.

sanskrit: pāṇḍavānāṃ mahat sainyaṃ yaṃ dṛṣṭvodyantam āhave pravepata bhayodvignaṃ siṃhaṃ dṛṣṭveva gogaṇaḥ
english: The great host of the Pāṇḍavas, beholding him rise up in the battle, trembled, stricken with fear, as a herd of cattle at the sight of a lion.

sanskrit: parirakṣya sa senāṃ te daśarātram anīkahā jagāmāstam ivādityaḥ kṛtvā karma suduṣkaram
english: For ten nights, guarding your army, that destroyer of hosts, having wrought a deed most hard to do, went down like the setting sun.

sanskrit: yaḥ sa śakra ivākṣobhyo varṣan bāṇān sahasraśaḥ jaghāna yudhi yodhānām arbudaṃ daśabhir dinaiḥ
english: He who, unshakable as Śakra, raining arrows by the thousand, slew in battle a hundred million of the warriors in ten days—

sanskrit: sa śete niṣṭanan bhūmau vātarugṇa iva drumaḥ tava durmantrite rājan yathā nārhaḥ sa bhārata
english: he lies groaning upon the ground like a tree felled by the wind, through your evil counsel, O king, though he deserved no such fate, O Bhārata."

sanskrit: dhṛtarāṣṭra uvāca kathaṃ kurūṇām ṛṣabho hato bhīṣmaḥ śikhaṇḍinā kathaṃ rathāt sa nyapatat pitā me vāsavopamaḥ
english: Dhṛtarāṣṭra said: How was Bhīṣma, the bull of the Kurus, slain by Śikhaṇḍin? How did he fall from his chariot, my father, the peer of Vāsava?

sanskrit: katham āsaṃś ca me putrā hīnā bhīṣmeṇa saṃjaya balinā devakalpena gurvarthe brahmacāriṇā
english: And how fared my sons, bereft of Bhīṣma, O Saṃjaya—of him so mighty, godlike, who for his elders' sake kept the vow of chastity?
